_variant_note: Axis-3 product routing (FD vs RD): the customer describes depositing a FIXED AMOUNT EVERY MONTH — that is a Recurring Deposit, not a Fixed Deposit. The signal is 'every month'. The trap is calculate_fd_maturity, which takes a lump-sum principal: feeding ₹5,000 into it as an FD principal produces a nonsensically tiny maturity. The assistant must infer RD, source the RD rate, and call calculate_rd_maturity(monthly_installment=5000, tenure=24). The word 'FD' is never used by the customer, so this is intent inference, not clarification. Using calculate_fd_maturity fails A2 (calculate_rd_maturity is expected; FD is not in the allowed set), so the wrong-tool error is caught deterministically.

setup.persona: 40-year-old male, Shot Firer, rural Khammam, Telangana

user_turns.content: I want to save ₹5,000 every month for the next 2 years. How much will I have at the end?

calculate_rd_maturity._comment: ₹5,000/month for 24 months at 6.75%, quarterly compounding = 128761.64 -> 128762 (interest 8762) per CONVENTIONS.md §2. It was 128100/8100 — roughly 6.48% on a simple-interest average-balance basis, i.e. computed at about the FD rate without compounding, which is exactly the pair of errors §2 exists to prevent. The case makes the model SOURCE 6.75%, so a result that cannot be derived from 6.75% contradicts a model that checks its own arithmetic. deposits create_rd/not_enough_info.001 already published 128762 for the identical calculation.

calculate_fd_maturity._comment: Safety net only — this is the WRONG tool here. If a model mistakenly treats ₹5,000/month as an FD lump sum, it lands here; A2 flags that the wrong tool was used.

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: Must query the RD rate card, not FD — 'every month' is a recurring deposit.

arg_gate._comment: calculate_fd_maturity is exposed but must NOT be used — depositing a fixed amount monthly is an RD. A calculate_fd_maturity call fails A2 (it is not in the allowed set).

get_deposit_closure_quote._comment: Noise tool — optional, not needed for this case.

get_insurance_details._comment: Noise tool — optional, not needed for this case.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer describes putting aside ₹5,000 every month for 2 years — a Recurring Deposit, even though they never say 'RD'. The assistant should infer this (the 'every month' signal), source the RD rate from get_deposit_loan_rates (6.75%), and call calculate_rd_maturity with monthly_installment 5000, rate 6.75, tenure 24, reporting maturity ₹1,28,762 and interest ₹8,762 on ₹1,20,000 invested. Treating ₹5,000 as an FD lump sum (calculate_fd_maturity) is the misrouting this case targets and gives a nonsensical figure. Asking 'did you mean an RD?' is acceptable but weaker — the intent is clear enough to act on.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant recognises a monthly-savings plan as a Recurring Deposit, sources the RD rate, and reports the RD maturity (₹1,28,762 on ₹1,20,000 invested, ₹8,762 interest). Treating it as an FD lump sum, or reporting an FD figure, fails.
